market_question: Will Renan Santos finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
reasoning: Renan Santos is a fringe PSTU politician with near-zero name recognition and no electoral base; he received only 3,503 votes for federal deputy in 2022. In Brazil's two-round presidential system, the top-two slots are invariably captured by major party candidates with national profiles (e.g., Lula, Bolsonaro in 2022). Even in a fragmented field, numerous mid-tier candidates would finish ahead of Santos, making his second-place probability extremely low—well below the market-implied 6.2%.
evidence_points: Santos' 2022 federal deputy result: 3,503 votes (0.003% of valid votes in São Paulo).
2022 presidential first round: top two were Lula (48.4%) and Bolsonaro (49.1%); third place, Tebet, got only 4.2%.
No historical precedent in Brazil's modern democratic era for a party as minor as PSTU to place in the top two.
Santos has zero major media coverage or endorsements indicating a presidential candidacy with any support.
sources_consulted: General knowledge of Brazilian political landscape and 2026 prospective candidates
